EESM 5000.title: CMOS VLSI Design
EESM 5000.description: CMOS process and design rules; MOS device electronics; CMOS circuit and logic circuit characterization and performance estimation; VLSI design and verification tools.  Project work will be centered on industry standard tools.
cilos: Recognize general architectures of social systems and networks.
Define data visualization, and process data for visualizations using some common tools.
Define fundamental graph theories for social network analysis, and process social media data for various applications.
Describe and explain the resistance and capacitance of transistors in a CMOS integrated circuit, and their relationship to output transition speed and power consumption.
Describe the dynamic switching behavior of CMOS integrated circuits.
Evaluate the speed, power consumption, reliability, and cost of a digital integrated circuit, and the tradeoffs among these four important design metrics.
Identify the principles of CMOS technology, basic fabrication process of integrated circuits, and CMOS technology scaling challenges.
Describe and explain wire resistance and capacitance and wire design optimization for achieving high-performance digital integrated circuits.
Define the operation principles of sequential integrated circuits.
Solve integrated circuit design problems by using computer-aided design tools and with team work.

EESM 5020.title: Digital VLSI System Design and Design Automation
EESM 5020.description: Structured design styles, specification, synthesis and simulation using hardware descriptive language (HDL), structural chip design and system design, circuit design of system building blocks: arithmetic unit, memory systems, clocking and performance issues in system design, design-automation tools and their applications, introduction to testing.
cilos: Recognize and explain the flow of designing complex digital system such as System-on-a-chip (SOC).
Identify the use of high-level hardware descriptive language in design digital system.
Recognize the design of the VLSI architecture for basic digital arithmetic building blocks.
Define the circuit and architecture design of different types of memory blocks.
Describe the techniques of designing low-power and high-performance digital circuits and systems.
Analyze, design, and debug simple digital systems.
Work in a team environment, and demonstrate effective project and time management through course design project.

EESM 5060.title: Embedded Systems
EESM 5060.description: This course introduces trends and design strategies for embedded systems. It will give a holistic view of embedded system design using smart phone as an example. It covers the basic hardware and software components involved in a complex embedded system. It also covers the design and use of System-on-a-chip (SoC) in embedded systems. The course will also discuss the design issues such as testability and power considerations. Hands-on experience will be provided.
cilos: Recognize and define the basic software and hardware components of an embedded system.
Recognize the anatomy of a mobile embedded system, and identify the key hardware of a smart phone and software components of a mobile operating system.
Analyze, design, and debug simple software and hardware components used in an embedded system.

Explain the interaction between the hardware and software components of a mobile embedded system, and the importance of integration of hardware and software components in optimizing the performance of the embedded system.
Work in a team environment, and demonstrate effective project and time management in lab sessions.

EESM 5100.title: Analog IC Analysis and Design
EESM 5100.description: Current sources, output stages, operational amplifiers, frequency response, feedback analysis, stability and compensation, slew rate, advanced integrated-circuit design techniques, analog VLSI building blocks.
cilos: Define the basic building blocks of analog integrated circuits, including current and voltage sources, single-gain-stage amplifier, multi-stage amplifiers and operational amplifiers.
Analyze and compute mathematically the behaviors of an operational amplifier, including voltage gain, response time, unity-gain bandwidth and power consumption.
Diagnose the stability of an amplifier and explain how to compensate the amplifier to achieve stability.
Design a multi-stage amplifier to meet certain constraints, such as supply voltage, power consumption and response time.
Use software tools, such as HSpice, to simulate the behaviors of a multi-stage amplifier.

EESM 5120.title: Advanced Analog IC Analysis and Design
EESM 5120.description: Noise analysis, advanced op-amp design techniques, analog VLSI building blocks, multipliers, oscillators, mixers, phase-locked loops, A/D and D/A converters, passive filter design, frequency scaling, active filter design.
cilos: Identify, formulate, analyze, and design Advanced Analog Integrated Circuits and Systems (amplifiers, filters, ADCs, DACs, etc.) for various applications.
Design and simulate Advanced Analog Integrated Circuits and Systems to meet target specifications subject to practical constraints.

Use appropriate simulation tools (including HSPICE, Cadence, Matlab, Switcap, etc.) to help design and simulate Advanced Analog Integrated Circuits and Systems with clear identification of their limitations and optimization.
Communicate effectively design choices and considerations via oral presentations and written reports.

EESM 5200.title: Semiconductor Devices for Integrated Circuit Designs
EESM 5200.description: Review of MOSFET characteristics, device modeling for circuit simulation (SPICE models), the BSIM MOSFET models, other semiconductor models, circuit model parameter characterization, design guard-band and statistical modeling.
cilos: Communicate with the language of semiconductor (diode, BJT, MOSFET, doping, Fermi-level, drift-diffusion, etc.).
Describe the basic principles of some common circuit active elements plus photo active devices (solar cell, LED, CCD).
Describe the effects of changing the key physical parameters of diode, BJT and MOSFET on the trend (increase or decrease) of the output characteristics.
Define the operation of a cleanroom.
Match a given model to measurement data by selecting relevant parameters.

EESM 5310.title: Power Management Circuits and Systems
EESM 5310.description: The course will cover power management circuits such as voltage references, linear voltage regulators, switched-inductor and switched-capacitor power converters; and power management systems for energy harvesting, RFID and bio-medical implants.
cilos: Identify, formulate, analyze and design power management integrated circuits and systems.
Use simulation tools to help design power management integrated circuits and systems.
Communicate effectively design choices and considerations via written reports.

EESM 5320.title: CMOS RF Integrated System and Circuit Design
EESM 5320.description: The course will cover radio-frequency (RF) system-on-chip using CMOS processes and circuit design techniques for wireless transceivers. At the end of the course, students should be familiar and acquire basic knowledge in transceiver architecture and integration, low-noise amplifiers, mixers, synthesizers, phase-locked loops, VCOs, and power amplifiers.
cilos: Identify, formulate, analyze, and design High-Frequency Integrated Circuits and Transceiver Systems for wireless applications.
Design and simulate High-Frequency Integrated Circuits and Transceiver Systems to meet target specifications subject to practical constraints.

Use appropriate simulation tools (including Cadence, SpectreRF, Verilog-A, Asitic, Momentum, etc.) to help design and simulate High-Frequency Integrated Circuits and Transceiver Systems with clear identification of their limitations and optimization.
Communicate effectively design choices and considerations via oral presentations and written reports.

EESM 5515.title: IP Networks
EESM 5515.description: Designed for students with or without background in computer networks, this course covers the basic layer model for computer communications, TCP/IP and related protocols, local area networks, and advanced topics in unicast and multicast routing, QoS, mobile IP, and security.
cilos: Recognize the key technological developments in networking technology.
Identify the fundamental principles for constructing a computer network.

EESM 5536.title: Digital Communications: From Fundamentals to AI-Native Networks
EESM 5536.description: This course introduces the principles of digital communication systems, covering signals, probability, information theory, coding, and modulation techniques. Students will explore communication over band-limited and wireless channels while gaining insight into AI-native networks, where machine learning enhances efficiency, reliability, and adaptability. By integrating classical foundations with modern AI-driven applications, the course prepares students to design, evaluate, and optimize intelligent communication systems for the evolving technology landscape.
cilos: Recognize the key technological developments in digital communications, including advancements driven by artificial intelligence and machine learning.
Identify the fundamental principles related to digital communication technology.
Perform basic performance evaluation and system design for digital communications, integrating machine learning techniques to enhance system functionality and efficiency.
Comprehend technical specifications and articulate how and why practical digital communications systems are designed.

EESM 5536.title: Digital Communications
EESM 5536.description: This course provides a comprehensive coverage of digital communication theory and design. Emphasis placed on system goals and trade-offs. Review of signals and systems, probability and stochastic processes; optimal detection of signals in noise; basic information theory concepts; coding; basic and advanced digital modulation schemes; signaling through band-limited and wireless channels; spread-spectrum communications.
cilos: Recognize the key technological developments of digital communications.
Identify the fundamental principles related to digital communication technology.
Perform basic performance evaluation and system design for digital communications.
Comprehend technical specifications and explain how and why practical digital communications systems are designed.

EESM 5539.title: Wireless Communication Networks
EESM 5539.description: Systems and protocols for wireless communication networks; from cellular to wireless IP applications, physical layer design for wireless systems with case studies, multiple access protocols, wireless networking technologies, evolution of wireless infrastructure for cellular systems, wireless network performance and link budget coverage analysis, packet data access and protocols, QoS for wireless multimedia.
cilos: Identify the design principles of wireless communication systems.
Illustrate the practical protocols of circuit-switched and packet-switched wireless cellular radio access networks.
Recognize the core network design and end-to-end protocol stack in cellular networks.
Describe and explain the protocol of WiFi IEEE 802.11.
Identify the future trends of wireless communications and broadband networking.

EESM 5540.title: Introduction to Telecommunication Networks
EESM 5540.description: Wired and wireless network structures, copper and optical access, transmission and switching, signaling and control, optical communications and wavelength networks, modern packet networking, virtualization, and the telecommunications business.
cilos: Identify the key components of the modern telecom network and describe their major underpinning technologies and working principles.
Effectively interpret scientific, engineering, and standard literatures related to the telecom industry.
Identify some of the major business sectors of the telecom industry and describe their operating characteristics.

EESM 5546.title: Wireless Communication Systems
EESM 5546.description: Overview of cellular structure and frequency reuse; mobile radio propagation and path loss models; statistical nature of radio channels; coding and time or frequency diversity; spread spectrum CDMA techniques and 3G Systems; OFDM and Wireless LAN standards; fast frequency hopping technology and Bluetooth.
cilos: Calculate path loss and receive power based on large-scale radio propagation models.
Describe the cellular structure and determine the frequency reuse factor.
Describe different small-scale channel variation models, and determine their key parameters.
Describe different techniques to combat frequency flat fading.
Characterize key parameters for antennas for wireless communications.
Describe spread spectrum techniques and their applications in 3G systems, and calculate user capacity for CDMA systems.
Describe the basic principles of OFDM and its application in WLAN.
Describe basic MIMO techniques, including spatial multiplexing and spatial diversity.
Analyze technical papers on an advanced topic on wireless communications and write a report.

EESM 5547.title: Multimedia Signal Processing
EESM 5547.description: Basic signal processing theory, image and video characteristics and processing, compression techniques, entropy coding, predictive coding, transform coding, vector quantization, subband coding, audio and speech processing, coding standards, real-time processing, watermarking, digital rights management.
cilos: Identify image and video characteristics.
Analyze and evaluate multimedia signal compression problems.
Integrate theoretical principles and practical implementations to solve multimedia signal compression problems.

EESM 5548.title: Mobile Edge Computing and Edge AI for 6G
EESM 5548.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction of Mobile Edge Computing (MEC), a key enabler of 6G networks. The covered topics include: communication and computation basics for MEC, computation offloading, communication and computation resource management, edge caching, MEC application scenarios, MEC hardware platforms and standardization. Edge AI is treated as a key application case, which is to support AI applications on resource-constrained devices with the help of MEC servers.
cilos: Identify the fundamental concepts of Mobile Edge Computing and Edge AI, including their architecture, principles, and key technologies.
Be familiar with the basic concepts and design principles of mobile edge caching.
Describe basic design principles of edge training and edge inference.
Analyze the integration of Mobile Edge Computing and Edge AI and evaluate their potential benefits and challenges in real-world applications.
Communicate effectively about Mobile Edge Computing and Edge AI concepts, technologies, and solutions through written reports.

EESM 5600.title: Photonics Technology and Applications
EESM 5600.description: This course introduces the fundamentals of photonics, as well as provides a survey on the frontiers of optics and photonics technology.  Fundamental topics include: geometric and wave optics, fiber optics, semiconductor light sources, and electro-optics.  Selected special topics include: biophotonics, micro and nano optics, photonic integrated circuits and components, optical switching and RF photonics.
cilos: Describe the fundamental concepts of photonics.
Strengthen problem-solving and communications skills.
Strengthen project management skills.
Identify current developments in photonics.

EESM 5620.title: Flat Panel Displays
EESM 5620.description: Discussions on various flat-panel display technologies. Emphasis will be placed on liquid crystal displays. Liquid crystal alignment and optics. Driving methods. Active matrix. Bistable displays. Plasma display panels. Inorganic and organic light emitting diodes physics and devices.
cilos: Define the basic optics and quality criteria of display devices.
Compare Liquid Crystal Displays (LCDs) with other Flat Panel Displays (FPDs), Plasma Display Panels (PDPs), Organic Light Emitted Diodes (OLEDs), etc.
Describe the physical properties of liquid crystals and preparation of liquid crystal cells for the most important applications.
Summarize basic electrooptical phenomena as a basis for liquid crystals devices.
Demonstrate how to control the liquid crystal behaviors in electric fields by varying its macroscopic physical parameters, cell geometry and addressing schemes.
Compare recent liquid crystal display applications in TV, desktop, PC, mobile, car, aviation, E-paper, etc.

EESM 5650.title: Digital Communication Networks and Systems
EESM 5650.description: This course provides an overview to the fundamental concepts in both digital communication networks and digital communication systems. Physical layer concepts of signal space and digital modulation are highlighted including M-ary modulation, OFDM and MIMO. Higher layers are introduced including MAC layer protocols such as IEEE802.11, internet protocols, routing algorithms, transport layer including TCP and local area networks. Approaches to analyzing and formulating digital communication networks and systems using these concepts will also be included.
cilos: Describe the key methods and technologies utilized in digital communication networks and systems.
Identify problems and trade-offs typically encountered in digital communication networks and systems.
Interpret technical specifications in practical digital communication networks and systems.
Calculate and assess the performance of digital communication networks and systems.
Formulate and devise digital communication networks and systems that can meet prescribed specifications.

EESM 5670.title: Advanced Architectures and Designs for Communication Networks
EESM 5670.description: Design and implementation of computer architectures; analysis and comparison of different architectures; fundamental concepts including pipelining, instruction-level parallelism, memory hierarchies, input/output architectures, and multiprocessing; modern issues including networking architecture, storage area networking, and VLSI scaling.
cilos: Explain the design principles of various modern communication networks.
Describe the detailed protocol of IP and wireless cellular networks.
Explain why communication systems are designed in the way they are in the industry.
Summarize the basic architecture of routers and switches.
Identify the future trends of the communication and computer networking.

EESM 5720.title: Signal Analysis and Pattern Recognition
EESM 5720.description: Computer-based interpretation of signals; temporal, frequency, and wavelet analysis; fractal analysis; object segmentation; data fusion; pattern recognition; density estimation; feature selection and extraction; clustering; dynamic time warping; hidden Markov models; examples from biomedical signal processing and speech recognition.
cilos: Identify the components required to build modern pattern recognition systems and their function.
Compare and contrast different pattern recognition techniques.
Calculate explicitly the decision boundaries resulting from a number of pattern recognition techniques on simple 1D and 2D data sets.
Formulate a pattern classification problem, and use software packages and datasets to build pattern classifiers.
Empirically compare and explain the effects of changing the hyper parameters of a classifier on real data.

EESM 5730.title: Modern Control Systems Design
EESM 5730.description: This course introduces basic concepts, tools and techniques for modeling, analysis, and design of modern control systems. The course starts from the use of differential equations and Laplace transforms to model continuous time systems. Then, basic tools needed for analyzing the behavior of dynamical systems will be presented. Finally, techniques for controlling their behavior will be introduced.
cilos: Model simple dynamical systems using differential equations.
Manipulate models of LTI systems in different forms, such as differential equations, transfer functions, and block diagrams, analytically and through the use of MATLAB.
Assess the impact of stability in a physical system and the use of feedback control to achieve stability.
Complete a real feedback control task from modeling, controller design, and simulation using MATLAB.
Identify robustness and performance issues in a control system and methods of addressing these issues.

EESM 5740.title: Stochastic Learning, Estimation, and Control
EESM 5740.description: This course will first cover the basics of linear state estimation starting from an introduction of deterministic and stochastic least square estimation. Then it will focus on Kalman filtering algorithm and its applications in remote state estimation. After that, it will introduce dynamic programming and optimal control (LQR and LQG). It will also present a brief introduction to Markov decision process and reinforcement learning.
cilos: Differentiate Bayesian and Non-Bayesian estimation and the associated MAP, MMSE, and ML estimators.
Identify the technique of completion-of-squares in deterministic and stochastic least squares and solve general quadratic optimization problems.
Recognize the need for and importance of linear state estimation and use the orthogonality principle to solve general linear estimation problems.
Derive the five core equations of Kalman filtering algorithm and explain their geometric and physical meanings.
Identify the dynamic programming principle and apply it to solve standard optimization problems involving additive cost functions and discrete dynamics constraints.
Describe the core idea of Markov decision process and how it is applied in optimal control and reinforcement learning.

EESM 5760.title: Integrated Design of RF Wireless Transceiver Systems and Building Blocks
EESM 5760.description: This course is to introduce design challenges and considerations of radio-frequency transceiver systems for wireless communication, covering RF concepts, RF wireless system architectures, and basic designs of their building blocks. Key blocks include phase-locked-loop-based frequency synthesizers, low-noise amplifiers, mixers, power amplifiers, filters, ADCs, and analog baseband amplifiers. Toward the end, integration of all blocks for complete integrated wireless transceivers will be discussed together with some comprehensive case studies.
cilos: Grasp basic concepts in analog and radio-frequency design techniques.
Describe design and integration of radio-frequency wireless transceivers.
Recognize design of key building blocks in the radio-frequency front-end, including inductors, low-noise amplifiers, mixers, frequency synthesizers, and power amplifiers.
Identify design of key building blocks in the analog baseband, including amplifiers, filters, and analog-to-digital converters.

EESM 5780.title: Diagnostic Medical Imaging
EESM 5780.description: This course introduces diagnostic medical imaging methods to graduate students. It covers the following topics: radiation, radiography, computer tomography, radioisotope imaging, diagnostic ultrasound imaging, magnetic resonance imaging, and applications of different imaging modalities.
cilos: Identify the concepts of radiation decay, projective geometry and their relationship in X-ray imaging.
Describe the Radon Transform, the Fourier Slice Theorem and their applications in CT image reconstruction.
Explain different nuclear medicine imaging concepts.
Explain the basic principle of ultrasound imaging and its applications in clinic.
Describe basic principles of MRI physics and imaging principles.
Explain applications of different medical imaging modalities in practice.

EESM 5790.title: Business for Electronic Engineers
EESM 5790.description: This course intends to provide engineering students with an introduction to the knowledge required in the conduction of business. Topics covered include: the organization of technology enterprises, fundamentals of financial and managerial accounting, engineering economics, operations and supply chain, quality processes, mindset of the marketer and the five steps of marketing, managerial finance, understanding of an enterprise from its financial statements, technology and entrepreneurship, and case studies.
cilos: Describe the basic principles and processes of business.
Determine accounting as the tool of measurement and control.
Identify the principles of managerial economics and decisions making.
Recognize the operation and supply chain process and the need of innovations and quality.
Acquire a marketer’s mindset.
Identify the principles of financial decisions.
Evaluate the performance of a company from its financial statements
Determine the technology life cycle and role of innovations and entrepreneurship.

EESM 5800.title: Modern Robotics: Theory, Development, and Case Study
EESM 5800.description: This course introduces the basic principles, development, and state-of-the-art of robotics. The course starts from the basic theory of robotics, including spatial descriptions, kinematics, Jacobians, and dynamics. Then, this course introduces the components and skills for robot development, such as actuators, sensors, control methods, and programming tools. Lastly, some state-of-the-art robotic topics for case studies, such as unmanned vehicles, humanoid robots, soft robots, micro/nano robots, etc.
cilos: Identify and apply fundamental robotics concepts, including spatial representations, forward/inverse kinematics, Jacobians, and dynamics.
Analyze and design robotic mechanisms and motion systems using mathematical and computational tools.
Select and integrate key hardware components such as actuators, sensors, and embedded systems for robotic applications.
Implement control strategies for robotic systems and evaluate their performance in dynamic environments.
Develop, simulate, and program robotic systems using modern development platforms and software tools.
Critically evaluate state-of-the-art robotic technologies and research through real-world case studies.
Demonstrate problem-solving and system integration skills through practical assignments and/or projectbased learning.
Communicate technical concepts effectively and work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams on roboticsrelated tasks.

EESM 5820.title: Emerging Technologies in Telecommunications and 6G
EESM 5820.description:
This course covers different emerging important topics related to telecommunications. Topics covered include 5G and 6G networks. Of particular interest will be the introduction of advanced technologies such as massive MIMO systems, advanced radio resource management (RRM) applications, integrated sensing and communication, cloud and edge computing, artificial intelligence (AI), Terahertz communication, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, smart grid networks, bit coin and security, inter-domain routing, Content-Centric Networking, Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and congestion controls in data center networks, 
and others.
cilos: Present a holistic view of different emerging topics related to telecommunications.
Recognize and identify the components of different emerging topics related to telecommunications.

Identify and explain the basic concepts and fundamental principles of emerging technologies such as edge computing, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, artificial intelligence, bit-coin security, and content-centric networking.
Identify the tradeoff between different designs of these emerging technologies.

EESM 5830.title: Engineering Thinking: From Research to Entrepreneurship
EESM 5830.description: This course aims to introduce students to the fundamental principles of engineering thinking and its application in research and entrepreneurship. Throughout the course, students will explore the creative process of generating ideas, formulating problems, and finding solutions through research. Additionally, students will learn how to identify the unique value of a solution and its potential for commercialization.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of the fundamental principles of engineering thinking and apply them to identify and solve complex problems in research and entrepreneurship.
Navigate the engineering research process effectively, including problem identification, hypothesis formulation, and solution development.
Explain the importance of intellectual property and the legal frameworks that protect innovations, including patents, trademarks, and copyrights.
Identify the unique value of engineering solutions and assess their potential for commercialization in the marketplace.
Create a comprehensive business plan that outlines the strategy for bringing an engineering innovation from prototype to market, including funding acquisition and branding strategies.
Analyze various funding sources and strategies for financing engineering ventures, including venture capital, grants, and crowdfunding.

EESM 5840.title: Introduction to Microsensors
EESM 5840.description: This course introduces microsensors that have become pervasive in the past few decades. The essential interdisciplinary topics in mechanical engineering, piezoresistance, semiconductor processing, etc., are introduced from the standpoint of an electronic engineer. A few major types of microsensors are treated in depth to illustrate the transduction principles, design, construction, fabrication, packaging, and testing. Finally, the course is concluded with sensor fusion and applications.
cilos: Perform the role of an electronic engineer in contributing to microsensor product development.
Collaborate effectively with team members across diverse areas of expertise, including mechanical design, IC design, sensor fabrication, packaging, and testing.
Demonstrate a solid understanding of interface electronics and system design for sensor applications.

EESM 5910.title: Topics in Telecommunications and Network Convergence
EESM 5910.description: This course integrates the MSc program materials together by covering one or more selected topics in the following areas: network convergence; multimedia and content delivery protocols; broadband signaling, and new IP signaling standards; mobile network and applications; other topics.
cilos: Analyze and evaluate the performance trade-off in voice over IP multiplexing systems.
Identify the technical issues related to voice traffic over the Internet.

EESM 6000-6009.title: Special Topics
EESM 6000-6009.description: Selected topics of current interest.  May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.
cilos: Analyze and evaluate the selected topics of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.

EESM 6900.title: Independent Study
EESM 6900.description: Selected topics in electronic and computer engineering studied under the supervision of a faculty member.
cilos: Examine a specific subject in electronic engineering.
Formulate one or multiple problems in the specific subject.
Integrate theoretical principles and practical skills to solve the defined problems.
Communicate the problems and solutions through scientific writings.

EESM 6910.title: Departmental and Professional Seminar
EESM 6910.description: Various departmental and professional seminars and workshops presented by postgraduate students, faculty or guest speakers. Graded P or F.
cilos: Acquire updated knowledge and skills in the related discipline.
Appropriately network with professionals.

EESM 6970.title: Guided Chip Design Project
EESM 6970.description: The class is designed to provide students with an experience of the complete IC design process in the industry from product definition to production and measurement. Taking a product in the market as an example, students are going to re-design the chip all the way from system definition, protocol design, selecting technology, installing technology file, digital building block design, analog building block design, digital analogy integration, ESD protection, post-design simulation, and tape out process. After that, the students will perform on-wafer testing, failure analysis, package selection, PCB design, test vector generation, reliability screening, ESD testing and data-sheet writing. Students completing this class are expected to have the equivalent experience of completing a full IC design cycle in the industry. May be graded PP.
cilos: Consolidate knowledge in IC design from different courses through a project.
Explain the complete IC design flow in the industry from specification to testing.
Design and implement digital and analog modules of an IC using industry-standard EDA software tools.
Present design solution using professional language of IC Design Engineers.
Identify trouble shooting and debugging issues in the design process.
Explain the industrial standard verification process after each step to ensure proper functionality of a chip.
Write the chip specification and testing report of an IC.

EESM 6980.title: MSc Project
EESM 6980.description: Independent project carried out under the supervision of a faculty member. This course may be run repeatedly for credit(s).
cilos: Consolidate knowledge from different courses through a project.
Recognize how a practical communication system is designed.
Explain why communications and networking systems in practice are designed in a certain way using theories learnt in various courses.
Present clearly and concisely how a technology is applied in practical systems.
